Jakob's Law (unverifiable here): as a web-based design tool Framer's desktop wrapper would inherit web-editor conventions (dense inspector, web type sizes), but no UI was supplied to confirm
notes: MARKETING-ONLY COVER, NO APP UI. macapp.supply payload = cover.png + icon.webp only (empty gallery, zero shot files). The cover is a brand composite (white folded-F mark on pure-black, ringed by ~18 third-party showcase-website thumbnails). Every thumbnail is an end-user WEBSITE hero (website buttons like 'VIEW PROJECTS'/'GET A QUOTE'/'Watch Reel'), NOT the Framer editor — verified by cropping. So NO UI rubric, native-tells audit, layout skeleton, or lineage-from-body was possible. lineage 'web-electron' is an EXTERNAL product-knowledge prior (Framer = browser-based website builder; desktop app is a web wrapper), NOT derived from the image — treat as low-weight, non-canon. rubric_score/native_audit_score set to 0 to denote not-applicable, not measured failure. Framer contributes NO macOS-native UI evidence to the corpus yet. Synthesis pass: do not cluster, do not promote anything, do not let brand tokens leak into UI/native canon. To advance, need a real Framer editor-window screenshot (canvas + layers/pages tree + properties inspector, light+dark). The icon.webp (charcoal squircle, white folded-F) was not digested (task scoped to Workflow A / UI only).
